name: Irbesartan
contraindications: Pregnancy (teratogenic risk with RAS blockade); bilateral renal artery stenosis; history of angioedema with ARBs
interactions: Concomitant NSAIDs (may reduce antihypertensive effect and increase renal risk), potassium-sparing diuretics or potassium supplements (risk of hyperkalaemia), lithium (increased lithium levels), other RAS blockers
monitoring: Check eGFR and serum potassium at baseline, 1–2 weeks after initiation or dose changes, and periodically thereafter; monitor blood pressure response and symptoms of hypotension
pregnancy: Contraindicated in pregnancy; stop as soon as pregnancy is confirmed and seek specialist advice
sideEffects: Common: dizziness, postural hypotension; metabolic: hyperkalaemia; renal function alteration; rare: angioedema
clinicalPearls: Well-tolerated ARB often used when ACE inhibitors are not tolerated; beneficial for proteinuric CKD but monitor renal function closely
indication: Hypertension (monotherapy or combination therapy) and reduction of proteinuria in chronic kidney disease; selected use in heart failure where indicated
